section_summary.extract_value: This section presents path analysis results examining the relationships between social safeness, body appreciation (measured with BAS-2), inflexible eating, and eating disorder psychopathology. A fully saturated model with 20 parameters was initially tested, followed by a readjusted model with two non-significant paths removed. The readjusted model demonstrated excellent fit and revealed that social safeness had a direct effect on body appreciation (0.35), which in turn had direct effects on both inflexible eating (−0.35) and eating disorder examination scores (−0.32). The analysis also identified significant indirect effects of social safeness on eating psychopathology mediated through body appreciation and inflexible eating.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents path analysis results from a single study (N=253) examining relationships between social safeness, body appreciation (BAS-2), inflexible eating, and eating disorder severity. Table 1 provides descriptive statistics and intercorrelations for all measures, showing a significant negative correlation of -0.36 between BMI and Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS_2). The path analysis reveals that social safeness has a direct effect on body appreciation, which in turn affects both inflexible eating and eating disorder symptoms.
